channel.title: ESSD - recent papers
channel.description: Combined list of the recent articles of the journal Earth System Science Data and the recent discussion forum Earth System Science Data Discussions

item.title: Age of smoke sampled by aircraft during FIREX-AQ: methods and critical evaluation
item.description:
Age of smoke sampled by aircraft during FIREX-AQ: methods and critical evaluation
Christopher D. Holmes, Joshua P. Schwarz, Charles H. Fite, Anxhelo Agastra, Holly K. Nowell, Katherine Ball, T. Paul Bui, Jonathan Dean-Day, Zachary C. J. Decker, Joshua P. DiGangi, Glenn S. Diskin, Emily M. Gargulinski, Hannah Halliday, Shobha Kondragunta, John B. Nowak, David A. Peterson, Michael A. Robinson, Amber J. Soja, Rebecca A. Washenfelder, Chuanyu Xu, and Robert J. Yokelson
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 8107–8127, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-8107-2026, 2026
Smoke age is an important factor in the chemical and physical evolution of smoke. Two methods for determining the age of smoke are applied to the NASA-NOAA FIREX-AQ field campaign: one based on wind speed and distance, and another using an ensemble of modeled air parcel trajectories. Both methods are evaluated, with the trajectory method, which includes plume rise and uncertainty estimates, proving more accurate.

item.title: CFDID: a China Flood Disaster Impact Database from 1994 to 2023
item.description:
CFDID: a China Flood Disaster Impact Database from 1994 to 2023
Shibo Cui, Ni Li, Shiruo Hu, Zhiqi Wan, Jiaru Wang, Jinchao Tang, Ruixi Zhang, Yingjia Li, Xinpeng Yu, Yiqian Tan, Wenbo Shan, and Jianshi Zhao
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 8129–8147, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-8129-2026, 2026
Floods have caused widespread societal and economic impacts in China, yet long-term and systematic records remain scarce. Using document scanning and large language models, we compiled and manually verified 1716 flood disaster records from 66 official documents covering 1994 to 2023. This open database provides a more complete picture of flood impacts in China than widely used international sources and can support research, disaster preparedness, risk reduction and insurance.

item.title: Analysis-ready European Groundwater Monitoring (EUGM) database
item.description:
Analysis-ready European Groundwater Monitoring (EUGM) database
Mariana Gomez, Héctor Aguilera, Julian Koch, Willem Jan Zaadnoordijk, Georgina Arnó, Montse Colomer, Benjamin Marchant, Bentje Brauns, Peter van der Keur, Klaus Hinsby, and Stefan Broda
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-748,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Groundwater levels across Europe have long been measured by many different national agencies. We gathered and cleaned decades of these measurements from 27 partners in 24 countries, creating one unified, open dataset of over 15,000 monitoring sites. This resource helps scientists study droughts, long-term water level trends, and build better models to manage Europe's groundwater resources.

item.title: ContrailStruct30: a 30 m three-band thermal-infrared dataset for contrail segmentation
item.description:
ContrailStruct30: a 30 m three-band thermal-infrared dataset for contrail segmentation
Jianing Yu, Lixing Zhao, Xiaoxuan Zhou, Liyuan Li, Xinyue Ni, Yuqing Xue, Kefang Wang, Ying Li, Guanzheng Du, Hanwei Lu, Chaoshuai Tan, Mingxin Dai, Zhuoyue Hu, Xiaoyan Li, and Fansheng Chen
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-759,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Aviation contributes to climate change through high-altitude cloud trails. However, tracking these thin clouds with satellites remains difficult due to a lack of detailed reference data. To solve this, we created a high-resolution satellite dataset to identify individual aircraft trails. Using advanced deep learning models, we showed that these trails can be mapped with precision. This work bridges satellite monitoring and climate research, helping build greener aviation technologies.

item.title: A near-real-time monthly dataset of CO2, CH4, and N2O emissions from fossil fuel combustion
item.description:
A near-real-time monthly dataset of CO2, CH4, and N2O emissions from fossil fuel combustion
Hanlin Niu, Jiaying Fu, Miao Huang, Xi Li, Xianhong Meng, Wenping Yuan, and Shilong Piao
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-848,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Fuel combustion is the largest source of greenhouse gases, but existing datasets either lag by years or cover CO2 only. We present a monthly dataset of CO2, CH4, and N2O emissions from fuel combustion for 153 countries and entities, by sector and fuel, from 1960 to 2025. Emissions for 2024 and 2025 are predicted from monthly activity indicators. The dataset supports carbon budget tracking, Global Stocktake assessment and near-real-time monitoring of sectoral emissions.

item.title: An open global reference dataset for natural and improved grasslands and its application for validation and area estimation
item.description:
An open global reference dataset for natural and improved grasslands and its application for validation and area estimation
Myroslava Lesiv, Steffen Fritz, Linda See, Stephen Stehman, Martina Dürauer, Ivelina Georgieva, Maria Schepaschenko, Leandro Parente, Radost Stanimirova, Laerte Guimarães Ferreira, Ana Paula Matos, Vinicius Mesquita, Ichsani Wheeler, Tomislav Hengl, and Lindsay Sloat
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-870,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
This paper presents a global reference dataset of 50,045 locations interpreted for 2020 using multi-source Earth observation imagery. It distinguishes detailed grassland classes and supports map validation and design-based area estimation. Testing a global map showed that improved grasslands are harder to identify than natural ones, and definitions strongly affect results. The data can help improve maps and support sound decisions about grassland protection and management.

item.title: The marine carbonate system in the northwest European shelf seas: a quality-controlled data product (NWESDAP)
item.description:
The marine carbonate system in the northwest European shelf seas: a quality-controlled data product (NWESDAP)
Margaux Brandon, Matthew P. Humphreys, Anna C. Koek, Marina A. Ádler, Dorothee C. E. Bakker, Meike Becker, Henry C. Bittig, Yann Bozec, Melissa Chierici, Elin Darelius, Helen S. Findlay, Thanos Gkritzalis, Ruth Ivimey-Cook, Elizabeth M. Jones, Marc Knockaert, Nico Lange, Coraline Leseurre, Helene H. Lødemel, Vlad A. Macovei, Evin McGovern, Triona McGrath, Nicolas Metzl, Garvan O'Donnell, Edel M. O’Sullivan, Yasmina Ourradi, Sébastien Petton, Anne G. V. Salvanes, Ingunn Skjelvan, and Yoana G. Voynova
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-872,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: upcoming, 0 comments)
NWESDAP (Northwest European Shelf Data Analysis Product) is a quality-controlled data product for the marine carbonate system in the northwest European shelf seas based on in situ samples collected during cruises and at fixed time-series stations from 1975 to 2026. The data product consists of 46,545 datapoints, compiled into a consistent format. The internal consistency of the data product is assessed through a rigorous quality control with uncertainties assigned for each component dataset.

item.title: Simulation database for impact studies of the NGGM and MAGIC gravity missions
item.description:
Simulation database for impact studies of the NGGM and MAGIC gravity missions
Marius Schlaak, Julia Pfeffer, Roland Pail, Marie Bouih, Alejandro Blazquez, Benoit Meyssignac, and Ilias Daras
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-672,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
In this article, we describe the ESA SING dataset. It consists of simulation results for future satellite gravity missions that measure mass transport on Earth. The dataset contains data products that display realistic noise behaviour, as we can expect from current and upcoming satellite missions. It allows users to gain early experience with data products from the next generation of gravity missions and to prepare to take advantage of the improved resolution that will become available.

item.title: A benchmark dataset of null-calibrated streamflow spectral-memory diagnostics for five CAMELS-family archives, with open rainfall-runoff model outputs for CAMELS-GB v2
item.description:
A benchmark dataset of null-calibrated streamflow spectral-memory diagnostics for five CAMELS-family archives, with open rainfall-runoff model outputs for CAMELS-GB v2
Lijian Ren
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-685,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Rivers carry a memory of the landscape around them, shaping how they respond to new rain. We assembled information from 3,010 river monitoring sites in five public data collections. For each site we measured how long this memory lasts and compared patterns across regions and models. Accounting for memory helped in some regions but not others. The dataset helps researchers test water models more transparently; the memory measure compares rivers, it does not show how water is stored.

item.title: The MioOcean Age Framework: Age Model Database and Chronoinformatics Approach for synchronised Miocene Ocean Temperature, Climate and Proxy Records
item.description:
The MioOcean Age Framework: Age Model Database and Chronoinformatics Approach for synchronised Miocene Ocean Temperature, Climate and Proxy Records
Anna Joy Drury, Deborah N. Tangunan, Diederik Liebrand, Gerald Auer, Jennifer Kasbohm, David J. King, Thomas Westerhold, Anya J. Crocker, Karlos G. D. Kochhann, Wolfgang Kuhnt, Diana Ochoa, Tim E. van Peer, Wout Krijgsman, Marci M. Robinson, Neeraj S. Shah, Elizabeth C. Sibert, Bridget S. Wade, Sindia M. Sosdian, Alexandra Auderset, Sevasti Modestou, and Ann Holbourn
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-724,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Reliable climate histories depend on knowing when changes occurred. We critically evaluated and harmonised the age information underlying global Miocene ocean temperature records, creating a consistent age framework, an open and updateable database, and a new approach for assessing chronological reliability. Our Chronoinformatics approach provides a transferable way to organise, evaluate and update age information for future climate syntheses.

item.title: MSM4D: a sub-daily soil moisture dataset with four nominal overpass slots from AMSR2-SMAP fusion (2015–2024)
item.description:
MSM4D: a sub-daily soil moisture dataset with four nominal overpass slots from AMSR2-SMAP fusion (2015–2024)
Mengran Wang, Peilin Song, Tianjie Zhao, Yongqiang Zhang, and Haigen Zhao
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-790,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Soil moisture can change within hours after rainfall, but most satellite products observe it only once or twice a day. We created a global 36 km soil moisture dataset for 2015–2024 by combining observations from two microwave satellite missions into four daily observation slots. The dataset greatly increases the number of days with multiple observations while remaining consistent with ground measurements, supporting studies of rapid wetting, drying, and other short-term land-surface processes.

item.title: A BPDF database retrieved using multi-angle, multispectral and polarimetric observations from POLDER-3 and DPC-2
item.description:
A BPDF database retrieved using multi-angle, multispectral and polarimetric observations from POLDER-3 and DPC-2
Zhe Ji, Zhengqiang Li, Gerrit de Leeuw, Cheng Chen, Yahui Che, Zihan Zhang, and Luo Zhang
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-834,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Earlier databases ignore the effects of atmospheric particles on polarized land signals. Using ground data and modelling, we processed two missions and built two databases. Ignoring particles changed the surface signal by over 10 % in 60–75 % of observations. Records corresponded under similar conditions nearly a decade apart. Coarser observations showed stronger land-dependent links between surface mixing and the signal. The method supports long-term records and atmospheric particle estimates.

item.title: SDUST2026SM: a global seamount catalog based on vertical gradient of gravity anomaly and bathymetric data
item.description:
SDUST2026SM: a global seamount catalog based on vertical gradient of gravity anomaly and bathymetric data
Yi Gao, Jinyun Guo, Shaoshuai Ya, Daocheng Yu, Xin Liu, and Cheinway Hwang
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-860,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Satellites can reveal underwater mountains where ship surveys are sparse. We combined satellite measurements of Earth's gravity with maps of seafloor depth to compile a global catalog of 67,374 seamounts checked by visual inspection. This is 55 % more than in a widely used 2023 catalog, especially for smaller features. The open dataset can help researchers study seafloor geology and plan future ocean-mapping surveys, though some small and deep seamounts remain undetected.

item.title: A high-resolution dataset of pre-rainfall low-level vertical wind shear derived from radar wind profilers across China
item.description:
A high-resolution dataset of pre-rainfall low-level vertical wind shear derived from radar wind profilers across China
Ning Li, Yongguang Zheng, Hui Xu, Tianmeng Chen, Xiaoran Guo, Linxi Zhao, Yuping Sun, Xuewei Cai, Honglong Yang, Liping Zeng, and Jianping Guo
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-866,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
To better understand how winds change before rainfall, we created a unique dataset from 28 radar wind profiler stations across China. It captures wind shear every six minutes during the two hours before rainfall. Stronger rainfall is preceded by a rapid increase and vertical shift in shear, while lighter rainfall shows steadier conditions. The data reveal changes missed by widely used weather analyses and may help improve short-term rainfall forecasts.

item.title: The Standardized Soil Moisture-Temperature Compound Index (SSTCI): daily scale global data set and event catalogue for compound dry-hot extremes (1961–2023)
item.description:
The Standardized Soil Moisture-Temperature Compound Index (SSTCI): daily scale global data set and event catalogue for compound dry-hot extremes (1961–2023)
Rukhshinda Aftab, Daniel Fiifi Tawia Hagan, Guojie Wang, Baoying Shan, Syed Husnain Shah, Zhou Chensi, Wei Xikun, Fareeha Siddique, Ali Hasan Jaffry, and Emmanuel Yeboah
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 7981–8002, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-7981-2026, 2026
This study provides a daily global compound dry–hot index (SSTCI - Standardized Soil Moisture–Temperature Compound Index) for researchers and a ready-to-use CDHE (Compound dry-hot extreme) catalogue for wider users, recording when and where each extreme event occurred, its duration and severity (1961–2023, 0.1°). Built on soil moisture memory and surface air temperature, they show CDHEs have become more frequent and longer lasting in many regions in recent decades, supporting targeted studies of impacts on water, ecosystems and agriculture.

item.title: Monthly-updated territorial fossil CO2 emissions estimates for Japan
item.description:
Monthly-updated territorial fossil CO2 emissions estimates for Japan
Taro Kunimitsu and Robbie M. Andrew
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 8003–8035, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-8003-2026, 2026
We present a low-lag dataset of monthly CO2 emissions from fossil fuel consumption and industrial processes in Japan, derived directly from official statistical data. The monthly dataset can be used to estimate the annual emissions a year ahead of the official estimates submitted to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC). Such monthly emissions estimates will provide further opportunities for understanding in a timely manner the reasons behind emissions changes, leading to targeted policy changes for climate mitigation.

item.title: Updated historical (1750–2023) trends of reactive gases and aerosols from the Community Earth atmospheric Data System (CEDS)
item.description:
Updated historical (1750–2023) trends of reactive gases and aerosols from the Community Earth atmospheric Data System (CEDS)
Rachel Hoesly, Steven Smith, Hamza Ahsan, Noah Prime, Patrick O'Rourke, Kalyn Dorheim, Monica Crippa, Zbigniew Klimont, Diego Guizzardi, Leyang Feng, Colin Harkins, Brian C. McDonald, and Shuxiao Wang
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-752,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Here we present an updated historical time series (1750–2023) produced by the Community Earth atmospheric Data System (CEDS), which is widely used in national and international models and modeling exercises. This dataset provides historical estimates of air pollutants and other gases. Aggregate annual estimates are available by 220 countries, 62 sectors, and 8 fuels (in addition to process emissions). Gridded data are also available.

item.title: Ten years of measurements (2012-2022) of the atmospheric composition at Saclay/SIRTA observatory in the Ile de France region as part of ICOS and ACTRIS
item.description:
Ten years of measurements (2012-2022) of the atmospheric composition at Saclay/SIRTA observatory in the Ile de France region as part of ICOS and ACTRIS
Laura Bouillon, Valérie Gros, Morgan Lopez, Nicolas Bonnaire, Carole Philippon, Camille Yver Kwok, Leslie David, Olivier Perrussel, Olivier Sanchez, Simone Kotthaus, Jean-Eudes Petit, Philippe Ciais, and Michel Ramonet
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 7941–7961, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-7941-2026, 2026
The Saclay observatory, 20 km southwest of Paris, monitored greenhouse and reactive gases, as well as aerosols, over 10 years to assess the impact of urban emissions. By comparing downwind and background conditions, the study revealed significant reductions in pollutants linked to traffic: -35.6 % for CO, -52.3 % for NOₓ, -56.7 % for eBC, and -15 % for CO2. These trends align with emission decrease estimates from AIRPARIF inventories over the same period.

item.title: MLAWind: a monthly sea surface wind dataset derived from an interpretable machine learning approach integrating in-situ observations and satellite data
item.description:
MLAWind: a monthly sea surface wind dataset derived from an interpretable machine learning approach integrating in-situ observations and satellite data
Weihao Guo, Rongwang Zhang, Xin Wang, and Dongxiao Wang
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 7963–7979, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-7963-2026, 2026
This study develops a monthly near-global sea surface wind dataset (MLAWind) from 1950–2023 through an interpretable machine learning framework integrating in-situ observations and satellite data. Evaluations show that MLAWind achieves comparable performance to the widely-used reanalysis datasets at different time scales. It provides reliable historical wind data during both satellite and non-satellite periods, demonstrating broad application prospects in ocean and climate research.

item.title: Network-based subbasin-scale mapping of streamflow alteration in Ontario, Canada
item.description:
Network-based subbasin-scale mapping of streamflow alteration in Ontario, Canada
Hongren Shen, Bryan A. Tolson, James R. Craig, Robert A. Metcalfe, Jonathan Romero-Cuellar, and James J. Luce
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 7915–7940, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-7915-2026, 2026
Dams and other water-control structures can influence rivers far downstream. We calculated the Streamflow Alteration Index for 245 576 subbasins across Ontario, Canada, averaging 4.3 square kilometres. By linking structure locations with connected lake and river networks, we mapped potential downstream influence, including places without flow measurements. This province-wide dataset supports river modelling, water management, ecological studies and targeted local assessments.

item.title: A global inventory of rock glaciers
item.description:
A global inventory of rock glaciers
Jinhao Xu, Min Feng, Yanan Su, Dezhao Yan, Qinglin Wu, Peng Zhao, Xuefei Zhang, and Xin Li
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-575,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Rock glaciers are widely distributed in mountain permafrost regions, but existing regional inventories are fragmented, inconsistent, and geographically incomplete, limiting global understanding. We developed the first globally consistent inventory using high-resolution satellite imagery, artificial intelligence, and expert review. This openly available dataset enables global comparisons and supports research on mountain permafrost, water resources, climate change, and environmental change.

item.title: NH-SDN: A Deep Learning-Derived Daily 0.25° Snow Density Dataset for the Northern Hemisphere from 1982–2025
item.description:
NH-SDN: A Deep Learning-Derived Daily 0.25° Snow Density Dataset for the Northern Hemisphere from 1982–2025
Li Zhong, Xueliang Zhang, Yuwen Lin, Dongyang Du, Yixi Bi, Liyang Sun, Yantao Liu, Jiale Geng, Sijie Zhao, and Pengfeng Xiao
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-689,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Snow density is an important property that influences snowpack conditions and their evolution. We created a new daily snow density dataset for the Northern Hemisphere from 1982 to 2025 by combining ground observations, environmental information, and a deep learning framework. The dataset is more accurate than existing products and better captures seasonal and year-to-year changes, providing valuable information for snowpack assessment and climate change research.

item.title: MioTEX: A comprehensive GDGT-based ocean temperature compilation for the Miocene
item.description:
MioTEX: A comprehensive GDGT-based ocean temperature compilation for the Miocene
Alexandra Auderset, Xiaoqing Liu, Neeraj S. Shah, Sarah J. Feakins, Francesca Sangiorgi, Amelia Shevenell, Kasia K. Śliwińska, Appy Sluijs, Evi Wubben, Yi Ge Zhang, Sevasti Modestou, Sindia Sosdian, and Ann Holbourn
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-711,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Climate models struggle to reproduce Miocene (23–5.3 million years ago) ocean temperatures, a period when CO2 levels overlapped near-future projections. Understanding this model–data mismatch requires evaluating available temperature records and uncertainties. We compiled MioTEX, a standardized global dataset of Miocene ocean temperatures from 46 sites using the TEX86 proxy. Calibration choices influence absolute temperatures. MioTEX is freely accessible via an interactive web platform.

item.title: Imaging the Ross Ice Streams of West Antarctica using active source seismology
item.description:
Imaging the Ross Ice Streams of West Antarctica using active source seismology
Huw Joseph Horgan, Andrew Robert Gorman, J. Paul Winberry, Sridhar Anandakrishnan, Howard Conway, Gavin B. Dunbar, Tina van de Flierdt, Denise K. Kulhanek, Richard H. Levy, Molly O. Patterson, and Ilaria Santin
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-723,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Knowledge of the past and future of Earth's ice sheets requires us to image beneath the ice surface and into the ice, water, sediment, and rock that lies beneath. An effective way of doing this uses active source seismology. Here we present active source seismic data imaging a diverse range of subglacial environments including subglacial lakes, sub-ice ocean cavities, and geological archives preserving the history of the ice sheets.

item.title: A long-term gridded dataset of the vegetation–atmosphere decoupling coefficient across the contiguous United States, 1982–2020
item.description:
A long-term gridded dataset of the vegetation–atmosphere decoupling coefficient across the contiguous United States, 1982–2020
Jinran Xiong, Han Chen, Wenli Zhao, Ziqi Lin, Chunmiao Zheng, and Yu Feng
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-732,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Long-term maps showing how vegetation and the atmosphere jointly control water loss from land have been lacking. We present a new dataset for the contiguous United States from 1982 to 2020 by combining observations from 74 field sites with environmental data and a computer model guided by physical principles. The dataset reveals clear differences across regions, seasons, and vegetation types, and includes uncertainty and quality information to support reliable climate, water, and land studies.

item.title: Species- and region-specific growth curves, forest age (2020), and disturbance trends for French forests at 30 m resolution
item.description:
Species- and region-specific growth curves, forest age (2020), and disturbance trends for French forests at 30 m resolution
Agnès Pellissier-Tanon, Yidi Xu, François Ritter, Nikola Besic, and Philippe Ciais
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-864,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
We created open data for mainland French forests to show, for different tree species and regions, how forests grow, how old they are, and how harvest and natural disturbances affect them. Combining satellite biomass and disturbance maps with national forest surveys, we map biomass growth with age, forest age for 2020, disturbance rates and biomass losses, and typical harvest ages. This helps explain the changing forest carbon sink and supports climate and management decisions.

item.title: CCWEM and CCWIF: 10 m Datasets of Coastal Wetland Extent and Inundation-Frequency Gradients across China
item.description:
CCWEM and CCWIF: 10 m Datasets of Coastal Wetland Extent and Inundation-Frequency Gradients across China
Jintao Liang, Yong Zhang, Yi Wang, Chao Chen, and Junfan Bao
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-758,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
We provide two open 10 m datasets describing China’s coastal wetlands in 2025. Together, they show both the maximum wetland extent and how tidal inundation varies within wetlands, offering a new national-scale spatial basis for wetland monitoring, ecological research, conservation, restoration, and coastal management.

item.title: A daily gridded dataset of nitrogen wet deposition over East Asia for 2011 to 2016 based on multisource observation-model fusion
item.description:
A daily gridded dataset of nitrogen wet deposition over East Asia for 2011 to 2016 based on multisource observation-model fusion
Nan Yang, Nuohang Liu, Baozhu Ge, Zhechen He, Yin Zhou, Danhui Xu, and Zifa Wang
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-857,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
We developed a daily dataset of nitrogen deposited by precipitation across East Asia for 2011–2016 at a resolution of 45 km. Combining simulations, satellite precipitation data and ground measurements improved agreement with observed daily nitrogen wet deposition. The dataset supports studies of short-lived nitrogen inputs to ecosystems and their contribution to total deposition. It also supports regional nitrogen budget analysis and model evaluation.
